intake.description: The claimant was admitted through the emergency department at a hospital for three days due to high blood pressure and a severe headache, incurring a bill of Rs 95,000.
intake.severity_reason: The claim involves an emergency hospital admission, and while it involves an emergency, the rule states severity is high if it involves an emergency hospital admission OR an estimated loss of Rs 5,00,000 or more. Wait, let's re-read the rule: 'Severity is high if the claim involves bodily injury, theft of a vehicle, fire, an emergency hospital admission, or an estimated loss of Rs 5,00,000 or more.' Therefore, emergency hospital admission means severity is high.

citations.quote: Inpatient hospitalisation: We pay for room, nursing, surgery, doctors' fees, tests and medicines during hospitalisation (HLTH-DEF-1.1), subject to HLTH-EXC-4.1 and HLTH-CON-5.1.

Pre-existing conditions: We do not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition (HLTH-DEF-1.3) until the insured person has had 36 months of continuous cover. This exclusion is amended by HLTH-END-6.1.
Diabetes and hypertension: For diabetes and hypertension only, the 36-month period in HLTH-EXC-4.1 is reduced to 12 months.

coverage.reasoning: The claimant was hospitalized for three days due to high blood pressure, qualifying as inpatient hospitalisation under HLTH-COV-2.1. Although high blood pressure is a pre-existing condition diagnosed in 2023 (within 36 months prior to the policy start date of 10 April 2025), HLTH-EXC-4.1 and HLTH-END-6.1 reduce the waiting period for hypertension to 12 months. Since the policy has been active for more than 12 months (from 10 April 2025 to 28 October 2026), the pre-existing condition exclusion no longer applies.
